title: The Mountain of Truth: from a Saxon mining town to Ascona, and out to the Brazilian south
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Mining Town and the Conservatory

stops.name: Freiberg, Saxony: the mining engineer's daughter
stops.date_confidence: attested; de.wikipedia and Wikidata Q16744619 both give Freiberg in Saxony, and the father's Bergakademie training fits it. it.wikipedia gives Freiburg im Breisgau, the outlier, and the discrepancy is recorded rather than hidden
stops.campa: A daughter is born to Raphael Hofmann, a mining engineer, and Luise Orges, in the Saxon town whose Bergakademie taught the father his trade. Freiberg lives off silver and off the school that teaches men how to find it; the ground under the house is worked out and shored up for hundreds of metres down. The mother's line is said to reach the historian Justus Möser and the geologist Bernhard von Cotta. They name her Ida. She will spend her life above ground, on a hill she buys herself, telling people what to eat.
suggested_refs: The Bergakademie Freiberg, where Raphael Hofmann trained

stops.name: Vienna, the family arrives
stops.date_confidence: year attested by de.wikipedia; the month and day are unrecorded and default to January
stops.campa: The Hofmanns leave Saxony for Vienna in the year Ida turns fifteen. The city is at the height of its music: the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde runs the conservatory that trains the empire's pianists, and a girl with an ear and a professional family can be placed in it. The mining town is behind her. Everything she will later refuse, the corset, the drawing room, the hired hour at another family's instrument, she learns here first, thoroughly, and to a diploma standard.
suggested_refs: The Musikverein and the conservatory of the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde, Vienna

stops.name: Vienna, the diplomas under Dörr and Epstein
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; de.wikipedia names Wilhelm Dörr, Julius Epstein and the two diplomas but gives no years and no institution. The Musikverein pin stands for the period's central Viennese conservatory, not an attested address
stops.campa: She studies piano under Wilhelm Dörr and music pedagogy under Julius Epstein, and takes a diploma in each. Epstein teaches at the conservatory of the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde and has had the coming generation of the empire's musicians through his rooms. Ida Hofmann comes out of it a certified pianist and a certified teacher, which in Vienna in the 1880s means a woman can earn her own bread without a husband. She earns it for the next decade, in other people's houses.
suggested_refs: Julius Epstein's teaching rooms at the Vienna conservatory

stops.name: Vienna, the hired hour in the noble houses
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; de.wikipedia attests the work but names no pupil, address, or year. Roughly a decade of her twenties is blank in everything reachable
stops.campa: She teaches piano in the households of the Viennese nobility, going in by the side door, sitting the hour beside a daughter of the house, going out again. It is respectable, it is precarious, and it is the exact arrangement her later pamphlets will attack: a woman with training and no property, selling hours to families that own everything and produce nothing. The Vienna years end when a post is offered her at the far southern edge of the empire, in a capital that is barely a village.
suggested_refs: The Ringstrasse palaces of the Viennese nobility, her clientele

segments.name: Cetinje and the Cure at Veldes

stops.name: Cetinje, the Empress Maria institute
stops.date_confidence: contested; one digest dates the post to 1890, but de.wikipedia says she was 'Anfang dreissig', in her early thirties, which puts it c.1894-1897. c.1895 is used and the conflict left open. The institute is identified as the Institut carice Marije by inference from founder and town, not by any source naming it with her
stops.campa: She takes a music post in Cetinje, capital of Montenegro, at a girls' institute founded under the Russian Tsarina for the daughters of high families. Cetinje is a settlement of a few thousand with a prince, a monastery, and a row of legations from every great power, the smallest capital in Europe and the most heavily attended. She is in her early thirties, unmarried, salaried, teaching Schubert to the daughters of a warrior aristocracy. The English literature will later call her a Transylvanian; the German never does.
suggested_refs: The Institut carice Marije, the Empress Maria Girls' Institute at Cetinje, founded 1869

stops.name: Veldes, the cure at Rikli's institute
stops.date_confidence: attested; her own memoir dates it to the summer of 1899 and names the Naturheilanstalt Rikli in Veldes. The coordinates approximate the Mallnerbrunn site on the lake's south shore and the precise footprint is unconfirmed
stops.campa: Her father falls ill and she comes to Veldes, on the lake the Slovenes call Bled, where Arnold Rikli has run a natural healing institute for decades on sun, air, cold water, and no meat. Rikli's patients walk barefoot at dawn and sleep in huts open to the weather. The regime is the whole of Monte Verità in miniature, a generation early, and Hofmann is inside it for weeks with nothing to do but take the cure and talk. She arrives a Viennese piano teacher visiting a sick man. She leaves committed to something else entirely.
stops.quote: Im Sommer 1899, gelegentlich eines gemeinsamen Aufenthaltes in der Naturheilanstalt Rikli in Veldes gewann mich Henri Oedenkoven für das in grossen Zügen geschilderte Zukunftsunternehmen.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (Lorch: Karl Rohm, 1906), p. 4; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD. The scan reads 'gelegenthch'; normalized.
suggested_refs: Arnold Rikli's Naturheilanstalt Mallnerbrunn at Veldes (Bled)
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 4

stops.name: Veldes, Henri Oedenkoven and Karl Gräser
stops.date_confidence: attested to the same 1899 stay; the month is a placeholder within that summer
stops.campa: Two men are taking the same cure. Henri Oedenkoven is the son of a Belgian industrialist at Antwerp, with money behind him and an illness that carried him to the brink of the grave and back again by way of vegetarianism. Karl Gräser, born 1875, is a former Habsburg officer from Transylvania who has thrown up his commission. In the huts and along the shore the three of them work out a plan: a cooperative settlement somewhere south, where the sun holds all year and land is cheap enough to buy outright.
stops.quote: Krankheit bis zum Grabesrande führte ihn auf den Läuterungsweg des Vegetarismus.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 4, on Oedenkoven; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD
suggested_refs: The Rikli cure huts at Veldes, where the founding group first met
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 4

stops.name: Munich, the founding meeting
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1900 by en.wikipedia; the day and the meeting address are unrecorded and default to the first
stops.campa: In October the group assembles in Munich to constitute itself: Hofmann and Oedenkoven, Karl Gräser and his younger brother Gusto, Ida's sister Jenny, Lotte Hattemer from Berlin, Ferdinand Brune. They agree to pool their personal property into a vegetable cooperative and to buy land with it. Gusto Gräser is twenty-one and already a wandering prophet; Hattemer is twenty-three and has walked out of a Berlin official's household. Seven people, one purse, and no site yet chosen.
suggested_refs: The October 1900 Munich founding meeting of the Monte Verità cooperative

stops.name: Munich, the free union
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; de.wikipedia dates the Reformehe to 1900, a year after Veldes, but names no place. Munich is used because the group did not reach the Ticino until later that autumn, so the common Monte Verità pin is impossible. In law this was a freie Ehe, not a marriage
stops.campa: A year after Veldes, Hofmann and Oedenkoven declare themselves joined in what they call a Reformehe, a reform marriage, and also a vegetarian marriage. No priest is asked and no registry is entered. The refusal is doctrine rather than convenience: they hold that love is a union completed freely in nature, and that the blessing and the state act are both impositions laid on it afterwards. Oedenkoven will marry Isabelle Adderley in law two decades later. Hofmann signs her book Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven.
stops.quote: Liebe, als eine in der Natur »frei« sich vollziehende Vereinigung zweier Wesen betrachtend, verwerfen wir für uns sowohl den priesterlichen Segensspruch als den Staatsakt.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 18; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD
suggested_refs: The Reformehe or 'vegetarische Ehe' of Hofmann and Oedenkoven, 1900
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 18

stops.name: Oberammergau, the road south
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; it.wikipedia and de.wikipedia place Oberammergau on the route from Munich to the Ticino in autumn 1900, with no day given
stops.campa: The party moves south out of Bavaria through Oberammergau, the village that stages the Passion every ten years and carves crucifixes the rest of the time. They are going into the Alps in October with their property converted into cash and no address to send it to. Behind them is a founding meeting; ahead is a hill nobody has seen yet. The route is one of the old ways over into Italy, and they take it for the reason every German before them took it: south, where things grow.
suggested_refs: Oberammergau, waypoint on the 1900 journey from Munich to the Ticino

stops.name: Cadenabbia, the lakes
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; de.wikipedia names Cadenabbia on the route without a date, and the month is inferred from the October departure and the autumn arrival at Ascona
stops.campa: They come down to the lakes and stop at Cadenabbia on the western shore of Como, in the belt of laurel and olive where the Alps end and the Mediterranean begins. This is the country they came for: palms standing in the open, lemons wintering outdoors, sun on stone in November. They look for land here and do not find what they want at a price they can pay. The search moves west over the mountains into the Swiss Ticino, to a lake with a hill above it called Monte Monescia.
suggested_refs: Cadenabbia on Lake Como, waypoint of the 1900 land search

stops.name: Ascona, the hill bought from Alfredo Pioda
stops.date_confidence: attested to autumn 1900 by en.wikipedia; the exact date of the first purchase is unrecorded and defaults to December. Pin inherited byte-identical from the corpus Monte Verità pin used by laban, suzanne_perrottet, hermann_hesse and charlotte_bara
stops.campa: Above Ascona on Lake Maggiore stands Monte Monescia, a hill of some three hundred and twenty metres. They buy it from Alfredo Pioda, a Ticinese politician and theosophist who had projected a lay monastery on this exact ground and never built it. Across several purchases the holding reaches four hectares. They rename it Monte Verità, the mountain of truth. Pioda sells them the hill and hands on the intention with it: what he sketched and abandoned, these seven will put up in wood within a year.
suggested_refs: Monte Monescia above Ascona, purchased from Alfredo Pioda in 1900 and renamed Monte Verità

stops.name: Monte Verità, the light-air huts
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1901 by de.wikipedia; no month given, defaults to January. Coordinates approximate the historic building cluster rather than a surveyed footprint
stops.campa: Building starts on the Licht-Luft-Hütten, the light-air huts: single rooms of wood with walls that open, set apart on the slope so a guest can sleep in the weather and wake into the sun. Casa Selma is one of them and still stands. The cure is Rikli's, carried over the Alps from Veldes and put down on a hill they own: sun, air, cold water, no meat, no alcohol, no tobacco, work in the garden, and a fee. The sanatorium is what pays for the commune, and it will be paying for it for twenty years.
suggested_refs: Casa Selma, a surviving Licht-Luft-Hütte of 1901, now a museum piece on the hill

stops.name: Monte Verità, Gusto Gräser put out
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1901 by de.wikipedia; no month given, defaults to June
stops.campa: Within a year the youngest founder is expelled. Gusto Gräser wants no fees, no guests, no accounts and no sanatorium; he wants the hill lived on and nothing sold from it. Oedenkoven and Hofmann are running an institution that has to earn its keep. The break is total and it is also local: Gräser does not leave the mountain, he moves down it, into a rock grotto below the meadow, where he is still squatting twelve years later when Rudolf von Laban's dancers arrive and take him for the genius of the place.
suggested_refs: Gusto Gräser's rock grotto below the Monte Verità meadow
laban.journey.json, Colegio Invisible atlas (shared Monte Verità pin)

stops.name: Above Ascona, Karl Gräser and Jenny Hofmann
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; de.wikipedia records that Karl Gräser and Jenny Hofmann set up separately after the 1901 split but gives no date, and no source consulted locates the parcel. Coordinates are approximate
stops.campa: The split takes a second pair with it. Karl Gräser, the officer who was at Veldes with her, and Jenny Hofmann, Ida's own sister, establish their own household on ground beside the colony. The mountain now holds three settlements within a few hundred metres of each other: the sanatorium with its paying guests, the Gräsers' plot, and Gusto in his grotto. All three are living the same doctrine, and none of the three will speak for the others. Karl will be dead by 1916.
suggested_refs: The Gräser and Jenny Hofmann property adjoining Monte Verità after the 1901 split

stops.name: Monte Verità, the name
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1902 by en.wikipedia for the formal constitution of the Sanatorium Monte Verità; no month given, defaults to January
stops.campa: The settlement is constituted as the Sanatorium Monte Verità. Hofmann is careful about the name in print: they do not claim to have found the truth, they claim to be working so that the lie is destroyed and the truth succeeds. The ground is dedicated by seekers, to seekers. It is a distinction the century declines to keep. Within thirty years the name is on a modernist hotel and an art collection, and within eighty on an exhibition catalogue about the hill's whole heresy.
stops.quote: »Monte Veritä« nennen wir den Boden unseres von Wahrheitssuchern gegründetes und Wahrheit Suchenden geweihtes Unternehmen.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 38; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD. Spelling and grammar as printed.
suggested_refs: The naming of Monte Verità, 1902, in Hofmann's own gloss
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 38

stops.name: Monte Verità, the woman question
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1902 by de.wikipedia; no month or press given, defaults to June. The title's word order is harmonischen before gesunden, which several digests invert
stops.campa: She publishes Wie gelangen wir Frauen zu harmonischen und gesunden Daseinsbedingungen?, How Do We Women Arrive at Harmonious and Healthy Conditions of Existence. The argument is the one her own life makes. A girl is raised estranged from any calling; she is offered maintenance in exchange for becoming a man's unconditional property; if she declines the bargain she enters the labour market untrained and fights men for the right to eat. The hill is her answer, and the answer is economic before it is spiritual.
stops.quote: In Folge so vieler unnatürlicher, ungesunder Verhältnisse ist ja das Mädchen heute gewaltsam seinem Beruf entfremdet [...] so begibt es sich in den furchtbaren Kampf um das Existenzrecht
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 5; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD. The bracketed omission is editorial, not a gap in the scan; scan reads 'unnatürhcher'.
suggested_refs: Wie gelangen wir Frauen zu harmonischen und gesunden Daseinsbedingungen? (1902)
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 5

stops.name: Ascona, hatless in the street
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the passage comes from the 1906 memoir describing the colony's early years and carries no date of its own. The year 1902 is inferred from its position in the narrative
stops.campa: They come down into Ascona to shop, and Ascona looks. The colonists wear loose reform dress and no hats, and their feet are bare or in sandals. In a Catholic fishing village on Lake Maggiore this is not a style, it is a public statement about God, property and the body, and the village reads it as one. Hofmann sets the sensation down in her book four years later without apologising for a line of it. The stir is the point: the colony is an argument conducted with clothing.
stops.quote: Unsere einfache und luftige Kleidung, unsere Hutlosigkeit, unsere entweder blossen oder nur mit Sandalen bekleideten Füsse erregten allenthalben grosses Aufsehen.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 10; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD. Scan reads 'xAufsehen'; normalized.
suggested_refs: Reform dress and the sandal at Monte Verità; the Ascona lakefront
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 10

stops.name: Monte Verità, Gustav Nagel in the snow
stops.date_confidence: day and month attested by the memoir, which names the seventeenth of November; the year is inferred from the book's narrative sequence. A de.wikipedia footnote credits the episode via TicinArte.ch, a domain that now redirects to an unrelated casino site and could not be checked
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of November, in heavy snow, Gustav Nagel walks up to the colony barefoot and dressed in a short shirt. Nagel is a German wandering preacher who lives on raw food and goes unshod in any weather; he is one of dozens who arrive on the hill unannounced because word has gone round that here this is normal. Hofmann's account of him is exact and unimpressed. She has built an institution with a ledger, and the prophets keep walking into it out of the snow.
stops.quote: Gustav Nagel tritt am 17. November vor unsere erstaunte Gruppe. Heftiges Schneegestöber hindert ihn nicht, blossfüssig und nur mit einem kurzen Hemde bekleidet einherzugehen.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 49; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD
suggested_refs: Gustav Nagel, wandering preacher, at Monte Verità, 17 November
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 49

stops.name: Monte Verità, Salomonson and the fruit
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1903 by de.wikipedia; no month given, defaults to January
stops.campa: The Dutch reformer Joseph Salomonson comes to the hill and argues her out of the last animal products. Hofmann goes vegan, in a year when the practice has no name and almost no practitioners, and the colony's kitchen follows her. The doctrine hardens as it narrows: exclusive fruit-eating is held to be the diet nature intended for people ripe enough in understanding to see it. Guests arrive for a rest cure and find themselves inside an argument about what a human body is for.
stops.quote: die ausschliessliche Fruchtnahrung als die ihnen von der Natur bestimmte und bekömmlichste Ernährungsweise betrachten
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 50; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD. Scan reads 'ausschhessliche'; normalized. Full clause restored.
suggested_refs: Joseph Salomonson and the turn to Vegetabilismus at Monte Verità, 1903
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 50

stops.name: Ascona, Vegetabilismus! Vegetarismus!
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1905 by de.wikipedia; no month or press given, defaults to January
stops.campa: The pamphlet Vegetabilismus! Vegetarismus! sets out the dietary case as the colony practises it, with the exclamation marks doing the work of the argument. Vegetabilismus is her word for the stricter thing, the plant diet without concession, held apart from a vegetarianism that still takes milk and eggs and calls itself reformed. She is arguing inside her own movement, against people who broadly agree with her. The distinction she is drawing will wait another forty years for its English name.
suggested_refs: Vegetabilismus! Vegetarismus! (Ascona, 1905)

stops.name: Ascona, the death of Lotte Hattemer
stops.date_confidence: attested; de.wikipedia, 'Lotte Hattemer', gives Ascona, 19 April 1906. The manner of death is contested and not resolved here: one account has a drug-dependent physician supplying poison, while the official police report of 1909 ruled suicide
stops.campa: Lotte Hattemer dies at Ascona at twenty-nine. She had come from a Berlin official's household to the Munich meeting of 1900 and had been on the hill from the first day, one of the seven. One account has a drug-dependent physician moving through the colony's circles supply her the poison. The police report of three years later calls it suicide. Johannes Nohl and Erich Mühsam are named in the rumour as well. The mountain of truth acquires its first grave, and no two tellings of it agree.
suggested_refs: Lotte Hattemer, born Berlin 24 November 1876, died Ascona 19 April 1906

stops.name: Lorch, Württemberg: the book printed
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1906 by the title page; no month given, defaults to January. The imprint is Karl Rohm at Lorch, not the 'Genossenschaftsbuchdruckerei, Ascona/Lugano' that circulates in some citations
stops.campa: Karl Rohm's press at Lorch in Württemberg prints Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung. Aus dem Leben erzählt, told from life by Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven. It is the founding document of the colony written by the woman who did the founding, six years in, while the place is still running and still solvent. She opens it with the resolve the founders took at Veldes. Rohm publishes theosophists, vegetarians and life reformers out of a Swabian market town, and this is the one book of hers still read.
stops.quote: Wahrheit und Freiheit in Denken und Handeln sollten künftig als teuerster Leitstern ihr Streben begleiten.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (Lorch: Karl Rohm, 1906), p. 3, opening line; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD. Scan reads 'Walirheit'; normalized.
suggested_refs: The Karl Rohm press at Lorch (Württemberg), publisher of the 1906 memoir
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), title page and p. 3

stops.name: Monte Verità, the mills that never came
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; the passage states a programme rather than a dated event, and is placed in the year of the book. The quoted sentence lies wholly on p. 7, not across pp. 6-7 as some citations have it
stops.campa: The book sets out what the colony is supposed to become. First the land and the huts, then mills, weaving shops and factories of every kind on a hygienic basis, built so that people can exercise their own abilities rather than heap up capital or unfold luxury, and finally schools to bring on what is in a person. It is a whole economy planned for four hectares. None of it is built. The hill stays what it was in 1901, a sanatorium with a garden and paying guests, and the programme stays on the page.
stops.quote: Späterhin folgen die Anlagen von Mühlen, Webereien, Fabriken aller Art auf hygienischer Grundlage zur Betätigung der individuellen Fähigkeiten und Wünsche.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 7; Internet Archive, MonteVeritaWahrheitOD
suggested_refs: The unbuilt cooperative economy of Monte Verità, as projected in the 1906 memoir
sources: Ida Hofmann-Oedenkoven, Monte Verità. Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p. 7

stops.name: Monte Verità, Hermann Hesse climbs up
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; hermann_hesse.journey.json dates his climb to April 1907 during a Locarno cure. Hofmann's presence is co-tenancy of the hill she owned and managed, not a recorded meeting; the Hesse file does not name her
stops.campa: Hermann Hesse comes up from a cure at Locarno and finds vegetarians, nudists, theosophists, anarchists and sun-worshippers resigning from the nineteenth century on Hofmann's ground. He is twenty-nine, newly famous, drinking more than his doctors like, and looking for exactly this. He does not stay long and he does not name the woman who keeps the kitchen and the accounts. The pattern is set here: the hill goes famous through its visitors, and its founders become the background of other people's conversions.
suggested_refs: hermann_hesse.journey.json, Colegio Invisible atlas (shared Monte Verità pin)

stops.name: Monte Verità, Laban's dance farm
stops.date_confidence: attested to summer 1913 by laban.journey.json and en.wikipedia. The end of the school's Ascona years is contested: de.wikipedia gives summer courses 1913-1917, en.wikipedia gives 1913-1918. No source ties Hofmann personally to the school
stops.campa: Rudolf von Laban opens his School for Art on the hill and holds it every summer through the war years. Mary Wigman climbs up from Hellerau; Suzanne Perrottet leaves Jaques-Dalcroze and follows her. They dance barefoot on the meadow at dawn because the colony has been doing everything barefoot at dawn for thirteen years, and they take Gusto Gräser in his grotto for the spirit of the place. Hofmann is on the mountain the whole time, thirteen years into running the ground they are dancing on.
suggested_refs: laban.journey.json, mary_wigman.journey.json, suzanne_perrottet.journey.json, Colegio Invisible atlas (shared Monte Verità pin)
Johann Adam Meisenbach photographs of the Laban school, Monte Verità 1913-14

stops.name: Ascona, the war scatters the colony
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 1914; suzanne_perrottet.journey.json records the international colony scattering as enemy nationals
stops.campa: In August the international colony that made Monte Verità possible turns overnight into a list of enemy nationals. Germans, Austrians, Hungarians, Belgians and Russians who had been eating at one table are now on opposite sides of a war, and Switzerland is neutral ground with borders and paperwork. Karl Gräser, the officer from Veldes who helped found the place and then left it, is dead by 1916. The guests stop coming. Hofmann and Oedenkoven keep the sanatorium open straight through.
suggested_refs: suzanne_perrottet.journey.json, Colegio Invisible atlas (August 1914, the colony scatters)

stops.name: Monte Verità, Isabelle Adderley
stops.date_confidence: reconstructed; de.wikipedia places the meeting and the marriage in the war years without a date or a place. Both the 1916 date and the Monte Verità pin are inferences from both parties being resident there
stops.campa: Oedenkoven meets the dancer Isabelle Adderley, born 1890 in India and called Bien. He marries her, in law this time, and they have three children. Hofmann, who declared sixteen years before that the priest's blessing and the state act were both impositions laid on a free union, watches her partner go and take the state act with someone else. The accounts say the three remain on friendly terms, and the arrangement holds: when the colony is sold, all three leave together to try the next one.
suggested_refs: Isabelle 'Bien' Adderley, born India 1890, dancer, second partner of Henri Oedenkoven

stops.name: Casa Anatta, Theodor Reuss put out
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1917 by en.wikipedia; no month given, defaults to June
stops.campa: The occultist Theodor Reuss stages a congress on the hill on nationalism, women's rights and mystical themes, and runs his own erotic rites alongside the programme. It is 1917, and Switzerland is one of the few places left in Europe where such a gathering can meet at all. Oedenkoven expels him. Seventeen years after the founding, the mountain of truth issues its second banishment, and the ground is the same as the first: this is an institution with guests, books and a reputation, and it will not carry a prophet who costs it more than he brings in.
suggested_refs: Casa Anatta, Monte Verità, site of the 1917 Reuss congress

stops.name: Monte Verità, Sang an die Sonne
stops.date_confidence: traditional; laban.journey.json dates the sun festival to August 1917 on the Monte Verità meadow, with a midnight station at Gusto Gräser's grotto
stops.campa: Laban and Mary Wigman stage Sang an die Sonne on the meadow, a sun liturgy running through the night to daybreak, with a midnight rite at Gusto Gräser's rock grotto below the colony. The land is still Hofmann's and Oedenkoven's; they have held it seventeen years and will sell it in three. Expressionist dance holds its founding festival on a vegetarian sanatorium's lawn, and the century afterwards remembers the festival, the choreographer and the grotto prophet, in that order.
